summary: Iteration 9 — Ingestion Core + Google Calendar Connector: FULL PASS. (1) In-process fake-mode suite tests/test_iter9_ingestion_and_google_calendar.py → 25/25 PASS in 2.55s (CALENDAR_PROVIDER_MODE=fake). Covers all 12 spec invariants a–m end-to-end via TestClient(server.app): OAuth start/callback-fake, ConnectorInstance upsert + cross-user isolation (404 not 403), AccessGuard (allow with active consent, 403 consent_denied on revoke), full Sync pipeline (initial ingest, dedupe→skipped, supersession on update, cancelled→archive backing node, malformed→quarantine w/o normalized_payload, two-calendar independence, cross-user isolation), Decision-generation flag (OFF: 0 decisions with metadata.origin=='ingestion:calendar'; ON: exactly 1 for 'Esame di matematica'-style event within 14d), revoke flow (status='revoked' + subsequent /sync → 403), audit redaction (event title UUID absent from /permissions/audit), CalendarContextProvider flag OFF (context_hash byte-stable + 0 signals.source_module=='calendar'), /context/decisions/{id}/latest 4-key envelope preserved, real-mode-without-creds → 503 provider_not_configured, ingestion/stats & /events shape. (2) Live-preview smoke test file tests/test_iter9_live_preview.py → 8/8 PASS against https://ora-decision-engine.preview.emergentagent.com in real mode: POST /connectors/google-calendar/oauth/start (auth'd) → 503 {detail:{error:'provider_not_configured', message:...}} — dict-shape confirmed; POST /oauth/callback-fake (well-formed body) → 404 'Fake callback disabled'; GET /instances → {items:[]} for fresh user; GET /ingestion/stats → {total:0, by_connector:{}}; GET /ingestion/events → {items:[]}; GET /connectors/registry — calendar_google now has status='available' (bumped from 'stub' as required); GET /connectors/registry/calendar_google → 200 status='available'. (3) Spot-checks tests/test_iter9_spot_checks.py → 3/3 PASS (fake mode, TestClient, real TOKEN_VAULT_KEY from backend/.env): invariant (a) instance doc contains 'sv_...' secret_reference and NEVER 'access_token'/'refresh_token'/'client_secret'; invariant (c) real mode + missing GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID → 503 provider_not_configured with dict detail; invariant (d) user B GET /instances/{A_id} → 404 (not 403). (4) Iter8 regression tests/test_iter8_permissions_connectors.py → 40/40 PASS in 12.17s. (5) Legacy suites tests/test_life_graph.py + tests/test_context_assembler.py + tests/test_auto_link.py → 86/86 PASS in 116.43s. GRAND TOTAL this iteration: 25 + 8 + 3 + 40 + 86 = 162/162 backend tests GREEN, 0 product bugs.

minor.issue: In REAL mode the endpoint is still REGISTERED and its Pydantic schema is exposed: malformed payloads (e.g. missing 'fake_account') return 422 with a full validation-error body before the mode guard runs (router.py:62-66 — the `if provider_mode!='fake': raise 404` check sits INSIDE the handler, so schema validation fires first). Well-formed payloads correctly return 404 'Fake callback disabled', so the spec test-text 'callback-fake in real mode → 404' still holds. Recommendation: conditionally exclude this route from the router at import time when CALENDAR_PROVIDER_MODE!='fake', or move the guard to a router-level dependency so 404 is returned before body validation. Low priority — no functional bypass, only endpoint-existence leak via 422.

test_report_links: /app/backend/tests/test_iter9_live_preview.py (NEW — 8 tests, live preview URL smoke + registry-bump guard)
action_items: OPTIONAL / low-priority: harden /api/connectors/google-calendar/oauth/callback-fake so REAL mode returns 404 BEFORE Pydantic body validation (currently returns 422 for malformed bodies). Two easy options: (a) skip include_router() of the fake-callback endpoint when os.environ.get('CALENDAR_PROVIDER_MODE','real').lower() != 'fake', or (b) attach a Depends() that raises HTTPException(404) before the request body is parsed. This prevents endpoint-existence enumeration via schema errors.
critical_code_review_comments: security/token_vault.py implements the exact abstraction pattern the spec requires: TokenVault base class (abstract put/get/delete), FernetTokenVault dev impl gated on TOKEN_VAULT_KEY, and a hard-fail VaultNotConfigured when the key is missing/invalid (verified empirically: an invalid dev key caused the whole callback to error out — no silent degradation). Secret refs use the 'sv_...' prefix and only the reference is persisted on the connector_instance doc.

connectors/google_calendar/provider.py factory reads CALENDAR_PROVIDER_MODE at each call site (provider.py:212). Real provider raises ProviderNotConfigured when GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/REDIRECT_URI are absent — NEVER falls back to fake. Confirmed via live-preview test: real mode + no creds → 503 provider_not_configured (dict-shape detail exactly as spec).

connectors/google_calendar/router.py routes are guarded consistently: /oauth/start catches ProviderNotConfigured and re-raises as HTTPException(503, {error, message}); /instances/{id}/* routes all funnel through a service layer that scopes on user_id → cross-user access returns 404 not 403 (verified). ONE nit: /oauth/callback-fake mode-check runs AFTER Pydantic body validation → 422 leaks endpoint existence in real mode (see backend_issues.minor).

ingestion/pipeline.py + normalizer.py + deduplication.py compose cleanly: pipeline drives per-event stages, dedup uses stable hash on (connector_instance_id, external_id, content_hash), supersession marks the previous IngestionEvent status='superseded' when content_hash changes (verified in test_d3). Malformed provider events (missing id) short-circuit to status='quarantined' with normalized_payload=null (verified in test_d5). Cancelled events archive the backing life-graph node instead of deleting (verified in test_d4).

context_assembler/calendar_provider.py is a strict no-op when CALENDAR_CONTEXT_ENABLED is unset — assembler still lists 'calendar' in provenance.providers_run but contributes 0 signals; context_hash is byte-stable across repeated assembles (verified in test_h1). Matches the pattern established by permissions_provider in iter8.

routers/ingestion.py + connectors/instances.py expose the minimum surface required by the spec: /api/ingestion/stats, /api/ingestion/events (paginated by connector_instance_id), /api/connectors/google-calendar/{instances,oauth/start,oauth/callback,oauth/callback-fake,instances/{id}/select-calendars,instances/{id}/sync,instances/{id}/revoke}. Auth is enforced via get_current_user on every route. Fresh-user shape confirmed live: /stats → {total:0, by_connector:{}}, /events → {items:[]}, /instances → {items:[]}.

Registry bump verified live: GET /api/connectors/registry entry for 'calendar_google' now returns status='available' (was 'stub' in iter8). GET /api/connectors/registry/calendar_google → 200 with same status.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter9 is FULLY green. To re-run in <3 minutes total: (1) `cd /app/backend && CALENDAR_PROVIDER_MODE=fake python -m pytest tests/test_iter9_ingestion_and_google_calendar.py tests/test_iter9_spot_checks.py -n 0 -v` — 28 tests, ~5s; (2) `EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=https://ora-decision-engine.preview.emergentagent.com python -m pytest tests/test_iter9_live_preview.py tests/test_iter8_permissions_connectors.py -n 0` — 48 tests, ~14s; (3) optional legacy: same env, `pytest tests/test_life_graph.py tests/test_context_assembler.py tests/test_auto_link.py -n 0` — 86 tests, ~116s. Field-name quirks (still valid): (a) google-session body key is `session_token`; (b) history events use key `event`; (c) auto-link proposals are per-decision only; (d) the GC oauth/callback response returns instance under key `id` (not `instance_id`); (e) TOKEN_VAULT_KEY must be a VALID Fernet key (32-url-safe-b64 bytes) — using an invalid dev placeholder causes VaultNotConfigured and the fake OAuth callback errors out (500-in-testclient-shape). The single low-priority issue to watch for regression: whether /oauth/callback-fake ever gets moved behind a router-level dep (would make malformed-body → 404 instead of 422).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no product regressions. Two test-authoring stumbles were fixed inline: (1) my initial spot-check hardcoded a placeholder TOKEN_VAULT_KEY that was not a valid Fernet key → the FernetTokenVault refused to initialize (security/token_vault.py:207) and the fake OAuth callback bubbled a 500 through TestClient's portal (masked as 'Event loop is closed'); loading the real key from backend/.env resolved it. (2) I initially expected the callback response to expose `instance_id` at the top level; the actual field is `id` per iter9 main-suite convention (test_iter9_ingestion_and_google_calendar.py:105). Both were test-only fixes, no product code touched.
